subject: [Urgent] BloxAI embeddings p99 spike after catalog update
messages:
From: Alex Cho <alex@bloxai.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: support@bloxai.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High p99 on embeddings after catalog push

Karthik,

We rolled the new model-catalog revision (v2027-06-20) earlier this morning and immediately saw the embeddings endpoint p95/p99 latency jump across several regions. Baselines went from ~45ms p95 / 120ms p99 to ~180ms p95 / 800ms p99 for our typical batch sizes. This is causing timeouts in our vector pipelines and impacting search freshness.

We've attached a short sample of request IDs and timings. Can you confirm whether this catalog change included the new quantized-v2 model variants? We need an ETA — this is affecting production traffic.

Appreciate any immediate mitigation (fallback to prior model, rate limits, etc.).

— Alex
Senior Platform Engineer
BloxAI

Attachments (referenced): sample-reqs-20270620.csv

---
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Cho <alex@bloxai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 on embeddings after catalog push

Alex —

Thanks for the fast heads-up and the sample. I'm escalating immediately and looping in SRE (Marissa) and CS (Vanessa).

Initial ask: can you send 3 request IDs (from the sample) showing the p99 tails and the approximate payload sizes? We'll try a temporary fallback to the previous model variant if possible.

What we'll do now:
- Marissa/SRE will triage traces and KV cache behavior.
- I'll check catalog rollout logs and routing policy changes.
- Vanessa will coordinate comms and SLA/credit asks if needed.

I'll update within 30 minutes with a mitigation plan.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 on embeddings after catalog push

Karthik,

Quick findings from the first 20 minutes of triage:
- The catalog push included a quantized-v2 candidate for the 'embed-small' family that landed in the hosted tier with default routing weight 0.6.
- Telemetry shows increased kernel invocation variance on certain GPU SKUs leading to tail amplification at long sequence prefixes (embeds with metadata). p99 spikes align with cache-miss paths.
- Trace dump attached (trace-logs-20270620.tar.gz) and perf CSV with request timing breakdown (perf-run-20270620.csv).

Short-term mitigation options (feasible now):
1) Roll back routing weight for quantized-v2 to 0.0 for hosted catalog (fast, low risk) — estimated 15–30m to take effect.
2) Apply a routing rule for BloxAI to pin to the prior quantized-v1 model (per-customer override) — estimated 45–60m to enact and test.
3) Tighten internal batching heuristics for embeds for affected SKU families — requires canary, 2–4 hours.

I'll start with option 1 immediately if you approve. We should preserve traces and artifacts for postmortem.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments (referenced): perf-run-20270620.csv, trace-logs-20270620.tar.gz

From: Alex Cho <alex@bloxai.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 on embeddings after catalog push

Thanks Marissa — that's helpful.

We confirm the problematic requests are medium-sized payloads (2–4KB) and the three request IDs we care about are:
- req_20270620_aa11
- req_20270620_bb22
- req_20270620_cc33

Please proceed with option 1 and keep us updated; if pinning is needed we'll take it. This is blocking our nightly syncs.

Alex

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: redwood-leadership@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Exec brief: BloxAI production p99 spike and mitigation plan

Team — quick exec summary for visibility.

What happened:
- A model catalog update (v2027-06-20) promoted a quantized-v2 variant that increased hosted embeddings p95/p99 for a customer (BloxAI) and other low-volume traffic patterns.
- Observed customer impact: BloxAI search syncs blocked; spikes ~800ms p99.

Actions taken:
- Marissa initiated telemetry triage and proposed three mitigations; we authorized rollback of quantized-v2 routing weight (option 1) at 10:20 PST.
- Rollback propagated; preliminary telemetry shows p99 dropping back toward baseline within ~25 minutes for affected SKUs.
- CS (Vanessa) is drafting customer comms and a credit proposal; we should consider a short SLA credit for BloxAI's impacted window.

Requesting approvals:
- Approve targeted rollback (already in flight) — low risk.
- Approve customer goodwill credit up to $12K for the incident window (Vanessa to finalize exact ask).
- Authorize a follow-up postmortem and a temporary freeze on promoting quantized-v2 to hosted until we validate under production traffic.

I'll coordinate postmortem and delivery of follow-ups. If there are objections or higher-priority asks, please reply-all. I will update in the 12:00 leadership sync.

— Karthik

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Alex Cho <alex@bloxai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-21T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: status, credit proposal, and next steps

Alex,

Thanks again for patience while we rolled back the catalog weight. Short update:
- Rollback completed and p99 returned close to baseline for your observed request patterns.
- We're proposing a goodwill credit equivalent to one week of embeddings spend during the incident window; estimate range $8K–$12K. If that looks acceptable, I'll route an approval request with Finance and Legal.
- Next steps: schedule a 30-minute post-incident review with our SRE and product teams; share the postmortem draft and mitigation plan. Proposed times: tomorrow 10:00am or 3:00pm PST.

Draft comms (snippet):
"We apologize for the disruption caused by a catalog promotion. We identified the root cause and reverted the change. We're offering a goodwill credit and will follow up with a postmortem and technical mitigations to prevent recurrence."

Let me know which meeting time works and whether you prefer a formal credit memo or direct invoice adjustment.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments (referenced): sla-impact-summary.pdf
